interpretations.text: Within the finite-budget native MuJoCo search, the best sampled control sequence had signed maximum excess J = 17.139436412481118, versus 20.426785753066465 for the baseline: an absolute reduction of 3.2873493405853473 in normalized excess. The worst best-sequence constraint remained holding speed at t = 0.45000000000000034 s: 0.3627887282496224 m/s against a 0.02 m/s limit. Thus the best sampled sequence still failed this diagnostic constraint by a normalized excess of 17.139436412481118. Holding speed decreased from 0.4285357150613293 to 0.3627887282496224 m/s, but holding maximum position error increased from 0.12402622706010982 to 0.15932031011406833 m; the terminal position error was 0.14882080641784826 m. These coupled changes do not identify a causal mechanism or establish an overall task improvement.

The search stopped at its iteration limit after 17 optimization evaluations and 17 rollouts (17,000 native physics steps), so convergence and global optimality are unresolved. The result is a valid finite-budget diagnostic failure, not proof of global, structural, or physical infeasibility. Independent task acceptance is unmeasured, and the evidence does not establish continuous-time compliance, whole holding-window compliance, hardware performance, robustness, repeatability, or equilibrium validity. It also cannot distinguish whether the remaining excess reflects control parameterization, finite search budget, local optimization limitations, or intrinsic model capability.

Missing discriminating evidence is a full 0-to-0.5 s replay of the recorded best control schedule under the independent frozen task-acceptance procedure, including every acceptance component rather than only the sampled native proxies. Evidence from broader or converged optimization would also be required before making claims about global nonlinear feasibility or infeasibility. Because the current run reached the iteration limit and provides no validated control sensitivity, it cannot support a structural modification direction or guarantee that an unvisited control sequence would improve the result.

The registered physical replay was a valid but failed task evaluation. Terminal position error was 0.14882080641784826 m against a 0.01 m limit, an excess of 0.13882080641784826 m. Holding maximum position error was 0.15932031011406833 m against 0.01 m, an excess of 0.14932031011406832 m. Holding maximum speed was 0.3627887282496224 m/s against 0.02 m/s, an excess of 0.3427887282496224 m/s; its normalized signed excess was 17.139436412481118 and it was the dominant recorded constraint. Force-bound violation was 0.0 N against 1e-08 N and solver errors were 0 against a limit of 0, so both passed. Thus the failure is an observed task-performance failure, not a solver failure or force-bound violation.

Persistent motion during the holding assessment is directly supported as the immediate reason for the holding-speed failure. At 0.45 s, speed was 0.3627887282496224 m/s, exactly the reported holding maximum, with tip velocity [0.16038542526505917, -0.12234582915617179, 0.3015355282476898] m/s. At 0.50 s, speed had decreased to 0.09020849285891432 m/s but remained 0.07020849285891432 m/s above the 0.02 m/s limit. The simultaneous position failures show that slowing by the final sample did not establish an acceptable hold. These observations do not identify why motion persisted: no diagnostic relations or recorded control diagnostics are available, and tension, controller, model, or transient effects cannot be causally separated from this execution alone.

Whether the observed failure is repeatable, robust, or structurally unavoidable remains unresolved. Only one physical launch was recorded, with no mathematical reintegrations, NMPC updates, or RL actions. The result therefore cannot establish global nonlinear infeasibility, structural infeasibility, continuous-time compliance, hardware performance, or whole-horizon behavior. Discriminating evidence would require additional registered executions or diagnostics that expose position error and control behavior over time; the sampled position-error field was unavailable at both cited times. No such evidence is present here, so no specific mechanical or control failure mechanism can be concluded.

C1.decision_use: Two/four-tendon screening, per-condition controls and a final 2.5 mm shortening comparison yielded one four-case structure.
C1.diagnostic_only: Initial mechanics/rank was diagnostic; four is the minimum successful tested count, not a global minimum; intersample overshoot remains.

M1.decision_use: Native full-window response search and independent three-condition replay; grouped anchors motivated a new structure and new controls.
M1.diagnostic_only: Finite search stagnation and local response ranks did not establish structural infeasibility.

M2.decision_use: External-load-bound Native control and strict unrounded hold-speed failure motivated same-source continuation with an internal search margin.
M2.diagnostic_only: The approximately 8.96e-16 m/s excess stayed a failure; optimizer margin never replaced the evaluator threshold.

M3.decision_use: The 0.50 s development task failed on the initial structure; a history-informed grouping hypothesis prompted rebuilt control and independent replay.
M3.diagnostic_only: Cross-task history was operator-selected; the draft protocol never became a formal benchmark.

M4.decision_use: Full timed reversal tracking search supplied the schedule for first independent replay and selection.
M4.diagnostic_only: No intervening structural comparison or additional mathematical diagnostic was recorded; no structural advantage follows.

M5.decision_use: Joint position and directed-axis search supplied a schedule; both original predicates drove independent selection.
M5.diagnostic_only: 54 callbacks were control search, not a separate mechanism study; axis success is not full 6D orientation.

M6.decision_use: Incomplete contact/numerical execution, then complete-but-failing material trial, motivated grouping and new loaded oriented control.
M6.diagnostic_only: Completeness, contact status and position/axis acceptance remained separate; comparisons do not isolate one cause.

P3.acceptance_level: development witness; 1/2-cell PASS; 4-cell INVALID; mechanism UNKNOWN at 4 cells
P3.decision_use: Static screening admitted c16 to dynamics; length/stability/ablation invalidity led to further finite comparisons and the frozen c26 witness.
P3.diagnostic_only: 1/2 cells passed, 4 cells INVALID; unstable means are not static convergence; invalid ablation is UNKNOWN.

PHS-2D.decision_use: KKT baseline qualification, modal/Jacobian screening and finite-load failures directed route/material/physical-guide comparisons; ten-condition dynamics established a development witness.
PHS-2D.diagnostic_only: Excellent row matching was insufficient under slackening; implicit modulus gradients were locally checked and did not establish dynamic performance.
